title: the artifact-door proof reaches its hook teeth on Windows, and names the teeth that need Linux instead of crashing past them
intention: test_artifact_door.py runs every tooth to the end on Windows: a tooth that needs systemd or cgroups is named red as unmeasurable here instead of aborting the rest, and the hook teeth reach the door in their scratch repos.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: on akiendell test_artifact_door.py reds all 14 declared teeth with 'aborted: FileNotFoundError' (also red at HEAD, baseline measured by swapping the two source files to HEAD); with teeth_callers stubbed, the remaining teeth run and 2 fail: the scratch hook says door not reachable, and the tester hook tooth's python3 reports no module cairn.tools.artifact.__main__
traces_to: Law 3 and Law 8: a proof that crashes past its own teeth on one platform measures nothing; Law 7: an unmeasurable tooth is a named red, not a silent abort; CP4.
how: Guard the Linux-only caller measurements (systemd-run, /sys/fs/cgroup) so on a box without them each such tooth records a named red 'needs linux cgroups' and the run continues; run the bin/cairn caller tooth through bash_script_argv; give the scratch repo's commits the environment the hook needs (CAIRN_REPO and PYTHONPATH, as the new commit proof does) and find why python3 cannot import cairn.tools.artifact.__main__ in the tester-hook tooth. Red-first is the existing proof red on HEAD.

clauses.claim: on a Windows box test_artifact_door.py runs every declared tooth to the end, each Linux-only tooth failing by name with the reason needs linux cgroups, none by an aborted FileNotFoundError
the two hook teeth, git commit of a journaled tree passes the hook and the tester hook asks the commit question first, are green on Windows
on a posix box the proof's results are unchanged

unknowns: how a Windows caller is classified (gate / akien / cc) is UNDECIDED: 3 teeth stay red, named UNRAN, until that is designed (a_process_under_a_transient_cairn_service_reads_as_GATE, a_live_process_in_a_login_session_reads_as_AKIEN, test_the_three_caller_classes_measure_gate_cc_akien); A.caller() returns cgroup None on Windows
the posix run was not made: the changes are guarded by _has_linux_callers() and os.name == 'nt', so posix behaviour is unchanged by construction only
the hooks join PYTHONPATH with ':' and Windows python splits on ';'; this is harmless on a live repo (cwd is the door) and was worked around in the proof, not fixed in the hooks
